question: Caffeine, the most widely used psychoactive compound found in beverages such as coffee and even some foods, is a ________ receptor antagonist.
solution:
The correct answer is __**adenosine.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caffeine, the most widely used psychoactive compound found in beverages such as coffee and even some foods, is an adenosine receptor antagonist.**
 
• Caffeine is a potent stimulant get from coffee and soft drinks.
 
• Caffeine is a psychoactive drug is found in tea.
 
• Caffeine is the world's most widely consumed psychoactive drug.
 
• The chemical formula of caffeine is C8H10N402**.**
 
• Caffeine is a **methylxanthine alkaloid found in the seeds, nuts, or leaves of a number of plants native to South America and East Asia **that is structurally related to adenosine.
 
• Caffeine can speed up the messages traveling between the brain and the body.
 
• Black tea consists of 50 mg caffeine per 220ml cup.
 
• Caffeine can reduce fatigue and drowsiness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uridine:**

 
 
• Uridine is a Ribo-nucleoside, composed of a molecule of uracil attached to a Furanose moiety.
 
• It is one of the five nucleosides that make up nucleic acids.
